rows.text: Feldon never actually reanimates anything. He makes a hasty TOKEN copy that is sacrificed at the next end step — so the body is irrelevant and the triggers are everything. The deck is built out of creatures that pay you when they enter and pay you again when they die, plus a small package of tricks that let you keep the token instead of losing it.

rows.name: Feldon of the Third Path
rows.text: {2}{R} and tap: a hasty artifact token copy of any creature in your graveyard, sacrificed at end of turn. Three mana for an attack trigger, an enter trigger AND a death trigger, every single turn.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste so he activates the turn he lands, and shroud so the removal aimed at him misses. Equip it before you tap him.

rows.name: Swiftfoot Boots
rows.text: hexproof instead, for when you need to target him with the Bracers.

rows.name: Thousand-Year Elixir
rows.text: haste for the activation and an untap, so Feldon goes twice a turn.

rows.name: Patriar's Seal
rows.text: mana, plus an untap aimed specifically at legendary creatures.

rows.name: Sting, the Glinting Dagger
rows.text: haste and a free untap at the beginning of EACH combat, which with an extra combat is a third activation.

rows.name: Illusionist's Bracers
rows.text: copies Feldon's ability every time. Two tokens per activation, forever.

rows.name: Battlemage's Bracers
rows.text: the same for {1} a copy, and it grants haste on its own.

guide.title: Bodies whose death leaves something behind

rows.text: This is the core of the deck. Feldon's token dies at end of turn no matter what — so use it on creatures that leave permanent tokens behind when they die.

rows.name: Wurmcoil Engine
rows.text: the token dies and you keep a 3/3 deathtouch and a 3/3 lifelink. Every turn.

rows.name: Triplicate Titan
rows.text: a 9/9 flying vigilant trampler that leaves three 3/3 Golems when it goes.

rows.name: Ancient Stone Idol
rows.text: a 12/12 trampler that leaves a 6/12 Construct.

rows.name: Myr Battlesphere
rows.text: four Myr enter with it, and the Myr do not die when the Battlesphere token is sacrificed.

rows.name: Solemn Simulacrum
rows.text: a land on entry and a card on death, every turn, for three mana.

rows.name: Ruin Grinder
rows.text: a 7/4 menace, and its death wheels the whole table.

rows.name: Dauntless Scrapbot
rows.text: strips every opponent's graveyard and leaves a Lander behind.

guide.title: Bodies with enter or attack triggers worth repeating

rows.name: Terror of the Peaks
rows.text: the payoff card. Every creature that enters under your control deals its power to any target — so Feldon making a 12/12 token is twelve damage to a face, and with a Bracers copy it is twenty-four.

rows.name: Balefire Dragon
rows.text: Feldon it, swing, and one opponent's entire board dies.

rows.name: Molten Primordial
rows.text: steal a creature from every opponent for the turn. Pair it with a sacrifice outlet and their creatures never come back.

rows.name: Duplicant
rows.text: exiles a creature on entry. Repeatable, unconditional removal once a turn.

rows.name: Meteor Golem
rows.text: the same for any nonland permanent.

rows.name: Combustible Gearhulk
rows.text: three cards, or three milled cards' worth of damage to the face. Milling yourself is upside here.

rows.name: Sandstone Oracle
rows.text: refills your hand to match the table's biggest.

rows.name: Ancient Copper Dragon
rows.text: connects for an average of ten Treasures.

rows.name: Daretti, Rocketeer Engineer
rows.text: returns an artifact from the graveyard on entry AND on attack, and his power scales with your biggest artifact.

guide.title: Getting the fatties into the graveyard

rows.name: Faithless Looting
rows.text: two cards deep, two fatties down, twice with flashback.

rows.name: Gamble
rows.text: finds anything. The random discard is often a bonus — you were going to want it in the yard.

rows.name: Wheel of Fortune
rows.text: a fresh seven and a graveyard full of targets. Best cast with a full hand of expensive creatures.

rows.name: Wheel of Misfortune
rows.text: the same, and it doubles as reach.

rows.name: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker
rows.text: a Treasure-making Goblin, then a two-card rummage, then a permanent copy engine on the back side.

cards.name: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker // Reflection of Kiki-Jiki

rows.name: Bitter Reunion
rows.text: discard one, draw two, and later sacrifices for team haste.

rows.name: Demand Answers
rows.text: two cards for a spare artifact or a fatty you wanted to bin.

rows.name: Fear of Missing Out
rows.text: a rummage on entry, and once delirium is on it grants an extra combat phase.

rows.name: Goblin Engineer
rows.text: puts an artifact from the library STRAIGHT into the graveyard, then recurs cheap ones. Fetch Wurmcoil Engine or Skullclamp.

rows.name: Ruin Grinder
rows.text: mountaincycles when you would rather have the land, which also puts it in the yard for Feldon.

rows.name: Monument to Endurance
rows.text: turns every discard into a card, a Treasure, or three life from each opponent.

rows.name: Jeska's Will
rows.text: a huge mana burst plus three impulse cards, and with a commander out you take both halves.

rows.name: Sundial of the Infinite
rows.text: end the turn in response to the "sacrifice at the beginning of the next end step" trigger and the token stays permanently. This applies to Feldon, Sneak Attack, Jaxis and Reflection of Kiki-Jiki alike.

rows.name: Sneak Attack
rows.text: {R} to put any creature from your HAND onto the battlefield with haste. With Sundial, you keep it.

rows.name: Jaxis, the Troublemaker
rows.text: a hasty copy of any creature you control, and the copy draws a card when it dies.

rows.name: Cursed Mirror
rows.text: a copy of the best creature on the board, with haste, and it is a mana rock afterwards.

rows.name: Altar of Dementia
rows.text: sacrifice the token BEFORE end of turn to mill on your terms, and it is how Molten Primordial's stolen creatures die permanently.

rows.name: Goblin Bombardment
rows.text: the same idea pointed at faces, and it turns every temporary token into reach.

rows.name: Skullclamp
rows.text: on the Myr and Wurm tokens, two cards each.

rows.name: Goblin Welder
rows.text: swap an artifact you control for a better one in your graveyard, every turn, for free.

rows.name: Daretti, Scrap Savant
rows.text: rummages on the plus, reanimates an artifact on the minus, and the ultimate returns every artifact that dies from then on.

rows.name: Scrap Mastery
rows.text: everyone sacrifices their artifacts and returns their graveyard's — and your graveyard is far deeper.

rows.name: Portal to Phyrexia
rows.text: three creatures gone from every opponent, then a reanimation from ANY graveyard every upkeep.

rows.name: Abrade
rows.text: three damage or an artifact, at instant speed.

rows.name: Untimely Malfunction
rows.text: an artifact, a redirect, or two creatures that cannot block. The redirect mode saves Feldon.

rows.name: Vandalblast
rows.text: overloaded it is a one-sided artifact wrath.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: cheap in a full board, and your value is in the graveyard anyway.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: mono-red's only answer to an enchantment or planeswalker.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it turns their removal into your removal.

rows.name: Tibalt's Trickery
rows.text: a one-mana counterspell when you genuinely cannot let something resolve.

rows.name: The One Ring
rows.text: a turn of complete protection, then it draws the deck.

rows.name: Imperial Recruiter
rows.text: finds Goblin Welder, Goblin Engineer or Feldon himself.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a discard outlet and a fatty. Faithless Looting plus Wurmcoil Engine is a better keep than Wurmcoil plus two more expensive creatures, because Feldon costs three and the graveyard is the hand.

rows.name: Feldon of the Third Path
rows.text: three mana, and he does nothing the turn he arrives without haste. If you have Lightning Greaves, cast him a turn early; if not, cast him with three mana up next turn so he activates immediately.

Use Feldon on death triggers before enter triggers when the board is stalled, and on Terror of the Peaks turns when you need damage. Wurmcoil every turn builds a board that survives the wraths this deck cannot answer.

rows.name: Sundial of the Infinite
rows.text: remember it exists. Keeping one Triplicate Titan or Wurmcoil permanently is worth more than three turns of temporary copies.
